number_of_offences: Charged under Section 69 of Army Act, 1950; upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the findings of the Court Martial and Armed Forces Tribunal that the appellant was liable to be convicted for the offence punishable under Section 69 of the Army Act for committing a civil offence of murder.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, including a Psychiatrist, and found the appellant guilty of murder based on the evidence presented.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant immediately came out of the tent, surrendered himself, and gave an explanation that he had fired the rifle under a delusion that there was a terrorist attack. His conduct and behaviour in jail, as per the Certificate issued by the Superintendent, District Jail, has been excellent.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 30.06.2003; Trial judgment: 21.08.2004; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: March 18, 2020
legal_representation: Mr. B.K. Pal, Ld. Counsel for the appellant; Mr. Vikramjit Banerjee, Ld. Additional Solicitor General, for Union of India
investigation_status: Challan registered before Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rajouri; case transferred to Army Authorities for trial; conviction confirmed by Court Martial and Armed Forces Tribunal
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction affirmed; High Court: Appeal dismissed; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed, sentence reduced to period already undergone
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant was liable to be convicted for the offence punishable under Section 69 of the Army Act, 1950 for committing a civil offence of murder.
defence_argument: The appellant contended that he shot the deceased in a delusion of a militant attack, wherein he was firing in retaliation, and had no control over his senses.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a proper sentence is the amalgam of various factors such as the nature of the offence, the circumstances of the offence, the prior criminal record, the age of the offender, the emotional and mental condition of the offender, and the prospects for rehabilitation.
precedent_relied_upon: Union of India and others v. Sadha Singh (1999) 8 SCC 375; Santa Singh v. The State of Punjab (1976) 4 SCC 190; Gopal Singh v. State of Uttarakhand (2013) 7 SCC 545
sentencing_rationale: The sentence already served by the appellant is much more than proportionate to the offence proved against him, and he has served more than 14 years of his sentence.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The appellant was posted in Kashmir during a period of terrorism, surrendered himself immediately after the incident, and has exhibited excellent behavior in jail.
other_sentence_order: The Court directed that the appellant be forthwith released from custody.
